title: Too small for a standard queen mattress & a hole in flat sheet. See the photos. Low quality.
text:
Too small for a standard queen mattress & a hole in flat sheet. See the photos. Low quality.. I love high thread count pure cotton sheets as a rule and if you get truly good ones that are actually made well from good quality cotton then they will last forever. These are not those sort of sheets. These are very soft and the dye is a true deep navy. However, these sheets are poorly constructed and they do not fit properly at all on a standard size queen mattress. SEE THE PHOTOS. The ends of the fitted sheet do not cover the entire mattress and leave a portion exposed. Plus the corner pocket seams are pulled so tight that the stitches are threatening to separate. My mattress is not extra thick or a pillow top and it doesn't have a topper on it.

Additionally, you need to make sure you wash these BEFORE you even think about using them. I always do, but some folks don't. Removing these from the package revealed a flurry of strings and excess threads of various colors and some dust. There is also a hole at the top of my flat sheet where the hem stitch wasn't finished correctly. See the photo. In time, with repeated use, this will rip. I washed them immediately according to the directions on the tags and they did survive that well with minimal shedding in the dryer. At best these are guest room sheets that will see little use a few times a year, but I will continue to spend my money on a known high quality brand for my master suite in the future.
